procnotices.notice_text:
GOVERNMENT OF SOMALILAND

MINISTRY OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT (MoLGUD)

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (REOI)

INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION

Country: Somaliland
Project ID: P508408
Project Name: Bulsho Project – Strengthening Community Institutions for Social Cohesion, Inclusion and Resilience
Consulting Service: PIU Bulsho Project Manager
Selection Type: Individual Consultant

Reference No: SO-MOLGUD-567780-CS-INDV
Duty Station: Hargeisa, Somaliland, with potential travel to the target districts and cities of the Bulsho Project
Duration: 12 months, renewable subject to satisfactory performance
Application Deadline: September 3, 2026, at 4:00 PM Hargeisa Time

1. BACKGROUND

The Ministry of Local Government and Urban Development (MoLGUD) of the Government of Somaliland is implementing the World Bank-financed Bulsho Project – Strengthening Community Institutions for Social Cohesion, Inclusion and Resilience (P508408).

The Bulsho Project provides initial anchor financing to the Government’s multi-year Bulsho Program, whose main objective is to strengthen community and local institutions for improved social cohesion, inclusion, and resilience. The Program places citizens and communities at the center of government action and supports decentralization, inclusive local governance, improved service delivery, community participation, and stronger citizen-government relations.

To support effective implementation of the Project, MoLGUD has established a Project Implementation Unit (PIU) and intends to recruit a qualified and experienced PIU Bulsho Project Manager to head the PIU and oversee the overall implementation of the Bulsho Project.

2. SCOPE OF THE ASSIGNMENT

The PIU Bulsho Project Manager will be responsible for the overall day-to-day management and implementation of the Bulsho Project, providing strategic leadership and supervision to the PIU and coordinating with MoLGUD departments, local governments, district authorities, communities, service providers, development partners, and other relevant stakeholders.

The Project Manager will oversee project planning and implementation; financial management and procurement; local governance and community-driven development; environmental and social safeguards; monitoring, evaluation and learning; stakeholder coordination; compliance and risk management; and sustainability and institutional capacity transfer.

The Project Manager will also oversee local governance and community-driven development processes, including participatory planning, Local Social Contract Platforms (LSCPs), Citizens’ Charters, community engagement, matching grants, community contributions, and community-level investments, ensuring that these processes are transparent, inclusive, accountable, and participatory.

The detailed scope of services, responsibilities, deliverables, reporting arrangements, and other requirements are provided in the attached Terms of Reference (TOR).

3. QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

The successful candidate shall meet the following minimum qualifications and experience:

  • A university degree in Governance, Political Science, International Relations, Public Administration, Development Studies, Project Management, or a related field. A Master’s degree in a related field is an advantage.
  • A minimum of eight (8) years of progressively responsible professional experience in project management, coordination, or implementation.
  • At least four (4) years of experience managing or coordinating large-scale government or donor-funded programs in local governance, institutional building, or service delivery, preferably in fragile or conflict-affected settings.
  • Demonstrated experience in community-driven development (CDD), participatory planning, and community-level implementation of development projects.
  • Demonstrated professional knowledge of the Government of Somaliland and Local Governments, including their structures, functions, and operational frameworks.
  • Experience working in fragility, conflict and violence (FCV) settings, with an understanding of local security dynamics and the ability to support implementation of security management plans.
  • Proven experience in decentralization, capacity building, institutional strengthening, and coordination across different levels of government.
  • Strong leadership and team management capabilities, with sound knowledge and experience in financial management, procurement, monitoring and evaluation, and stakeholder engagement.
  • Strong negotiation, organizational, communication, representation, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to deliver effectively under pressure.
  • Demonstrated commitment to gender and social inclusion and engagement of marginalized groups, including women, youth, minority groups, and IDPs.
  • High standards of integrity, ethical conduct, professional accountability, and leadership.
  • In-depth knowledge of Somaliland’s governance structures, political dynamics, and local context, and familiarity with international development partners working in community development, social cohesion, and local governance.
  • Proficiency in relevant project management tools and software.
  • Excellent command of English and Somali, including reading, writing, communication, and presentation skills.

4. REPORTING AND DURATION

The PIU Bulsho Project Manager will report administratively to the Director General of the Ministry of Local Government and Urban Development (MoLGUD).

The assignment will initially be for 12 months and may be renewed subject to satisfactory performance and project requirements. The duty station is Hargeisa, Somaliland, with potential travel to the target districts and cities of the Bulsho Project.

5. SELECTION METHOD

The Ministry of Local Government and Urban Development (MoLGUD), Government of Somaliland, now invites eligible and qualified Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the above-mentioned services.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Project Financing – Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020 and September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations and applicable Government of Somaliland policies.

 

 

6. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS

Interested Consultants should submit:

  1. A detailed and updated Curriculum Vitae (CV), including contact details of three (3) professional referees;
  2. Copies of relevant academic qualification certificates; and
  3. A cover letter outlining the candidate’s relevant experience and qualifications in relation to the assignment.

Interested and qualified candidates should submit their applications by email with the subject line:

“Application for PIU Bulsho Project Manager – SO-MOLGUD-567780-CS-INDV”

To: bulsho.somaliland@outlook.com
Cc: dg.molgud@sldgov.org

Applications must be received no later than September 3, 2026, at 4:00 PM Hargeisa Time.

Attention:

PIU Bulsho Project Manager Recruitment
Bulsho Project – Strengthening Community Institutions for Social Cohesion, Inclusion and Resilience
Ministry of Local Government and Urban Development (MoLGUD)
Government of Somaliland
Hargeisa, Somaliland

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this REOI.

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(Consulting Services – Firm Selection)

 

Date of Issue:  14th August 2026

Country: Republic of Sierra Leone

Name of Project:  Sierra Leone Digital Transformation Project

 

Consulting Services: Recruitment of a Consulting Firm for the Implementation and Operationalization of a License-Free National Multi-Hazard Early Warning System (MHEWS). Ref: SL-MoF-565234-CS-QCBS

 

    1. Introduction

The Government of Sierra Leone (GoSL) has committed to transforming its economy based on a more inclusive and human-centric digital growth and development approach. A high-level vision for the digital economy is articulated in the new National Digital Development Policy (NDDP), which was approved by the Cabinet in December 2021 setting the GoSL’s vision to transform Sierra Leone into an inclusive digital economy and society and to leverage digital technology to support the GoSL to deliver on its national development plan effectively and efficiently. The Sierra Leone Digital Transformation Project (SLDTP) aims to expand access to broadband internet, increase digital skills, and improve government capacity to deliver public services digitally. The project will support the development of a strong enabling environment for the nation’s digital transformation and digital development agenda as articulated in the National Digital Development Strategy.

 

    1. Objectives

The general objective of this assignment is to design, customize, implement, and operationalize a national, end-to-end MHEWS for Sierra Leone that enables NDMA and its partner institutions to effectively manage the full early warning value chain, from risk knowledge and hazard monitoring to warning dissemination and coordinated preparedness and response, using a license-free, sustainable, and nationally owned digital platform. The implemented system shall translate the technical recommendations, blueprint, and SRS into a fully functional, interoperable, and people-centred solution that strengthens disaster risk reduction, protects lives and livelihoods, and supports timely early action.

  1. Specific Objectives

The specific objectives of the assignment are to:

  • Configure and customize an existing, license-free EWS application (open-source or equivalent) to fully meet the functional and technical requirements defined in the approved blueprint and SRS, without developing a system from scratch.
  • Implement an integrated national EWS platform that operationalizes all four pillars of a MHEWS:
    • Risk Knowledge
    • Detection, Monitoring and Forecasting
    • Warning Dissemination and Communication
    • Preparedness and Response
  • Implement the MHEWS using a phased implementation approach, beginning with a priority hazard to validate system functionality, data-sharing workflows, and warning dissemination mechanisms before expanding the system to additional hazards, datasets, and dissemination channels.
  • Establish a centralized decision-support and early warning platform anchored at the National Emergency Operations Centre (NEOC), with secure connectivity to District Emergency Operations Centres (DEOCs) and community-level structures.
  • Enable real-time and near-real-time data integration from multiple hazard monitoring systems, sector institutions, and external data sources, supporting automated analysis, forecasting, and impact-based decision-making.
  • Operationalize a Common Alerting Protocol (CAP)–compliant national alerting system that serves as the single authoritative source for public warnings and supports multi-channel dissemination, including digital, telecom, media, and community-based channels.
  • Ensure inclusive, people-centred warning delivery, including accessibility features for persons with disabilities, and mechanisms to reach at-risk populations in remote and low-connectivity areas.
  • Strengthen preparedness and response coordination by providing digital tools for incident management, forecast-to-action workflows, resource tracking, situation reporting, drills, and after-action review.
  • Ensure interoperability with existing national digital platforms and sector systems, using open standards and APIs, and leveraging the hosting environment provided by MoCTI.
  • Implement robust security, role-based access control, audit trails, and governance mechanisms to protect the integrity, authenticity, and reliability of life-critical warning information.
  • Design and operationalize integrated data-sharing protocols between NDMA and relevant national institutions to support effective early warning operations. This shall include the definition and implementation of data governance and access protocols; interoperability standards and application programming interfaces (APIs); secure real-time and near-real-time data exchange mechanisms; and clearly defined roles and responsibilities of participating institutions. The assignment shall also support the development of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to govern operational workflows for the MHEWS, including protocols for validating and acting upon field reports and community acknowledgements, alert generation and approval processes, inter-agency coordination during emergencies, and procedures for warning dissemination through telecom operators, broadcasters, and other communication channels. The data-sharing framework shall enable timely, accurate, and secure dissemination of disaster-related information to NDMA decision-makers, partner institutions, and the public, in line with national governance arrangements and security requirements.
  • Build institutional capacity and ensure sustainability through comprehensive documentation, training, knowledge transfer, and handover, enabling NDMA to fully own, manage, maintain, and expand the system without reliance on proprietary licenses or vendor lock-in.
  • Deliver a fully tested, accepted, and operational EWS that complies with national policies and international best practices for multi-hazard early warning systems and supports Sierra Leone’s commitments to disaster risk reduction and early warnings for all.

The Project Coordination Unit of the Sierra Leone Digital Transformation Project now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are core business and years in business, relevant experience, and technical and managerial capability of the firm. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers July 2016 Revised September 2025 Seventh Edition, and National Public Procurement Act 2016, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. Eswatini Electricity Company (EEC)

 

(Government of the Kingdom of Eswatini)

Consultancy Services for the Development of a National Clean Cooking Transition Strategy and Costed Implementation Plan

 

First date of publication:           17 August 2026

Country:                                      Kingdom of Eswatini

Name of Project:                        Accelerating Sustainable and Clean Energy Access Transformation in Eswatini (ASCENT Eswatini) Project

Sector:                                          Energy Sector

Credit No:                                   IDA-7700-SZ

Project ID No.:                            P508960

Assignment Title:                       Consultancy Services For the development of a National Clean Cooking Transition Strategy and Implementation plan for the Kingdom of Eswatini.

Reference No.                              SZ-ECC-561941-CS-QCBS

 

  1. The Government of the Kingdom of Eswatini (GoKE), through the Ministry of Natural Resources and Energy (MNRE), and with the Eswatini Electricity Company (EEC) as the implementing agency is implementing the Accelerating Sustainable and Clean Energy Access Transformation in Eswatini (ASCENT Eswatini) Project. As part of its commitment to achieving universal access to modern energy services under Mission 300 and accelerating the transition away from traditional biomass, the Government intends to develop a National Clean Cooking Transition Strategy and Costed Implementation Plan. The Strategy will provide a comprehensive, evidence-based roadmap for increasing access to affordable, reliable and sustainable clean cooking solutions for households, institutions and commercial users, while strengthening policy, regulatory, market, financing and institutional frameworks. The MNRE now seeks to engage a qualified consulting firm or consortium to undertake this assignment. This assignment will also contribute to the implementation of the National Energy Compact.

 

  1. The consulting services ("the Services") will include, but not be limited to, the following workstreams:

a. Situational, institutional and market assessment for clean cooking.

b. Policy, legal, regulatory and institutional review.

c. Infrastructure, supply chain and clean cooking technology assessment, including electric cooking.

d. Household, institutional and commercial demand assessment, including affordability and consumer behaviour.

e. Financing, investment and carbon finance assessment.

f. Environmental, climate, health, gender and social inclusion assessment.

g. Development of the National Clean Cooking Transition Strategy, Costed Implementation Plan and Investment and Financing Roadmap.

h. Stakeholder consultations, validation workshops and knowledge transfer.

 

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the primary procurement stage for the assignment can be obtained from the EEC and the MNRE upon request or downloaded from: TERMS_OF_REFERENCE_CLEAN_COOKING_FINAL.pdf

 

  1. Interested consultants must provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform all the services. The following documents shall also be submitted along with the EOI applications by all consulting firms, including each member of JV firms:
      1. Copies Certificate of incorporation/registration.
      2. Company profile.
      3. Organisational structure.
      4. Quality assurance arrangements.
      5. Availability of key technical staff.
      6. Information on software, modelling tools and analytical capacity relevant to the assignment.

 

  1. The short-listing criteria are:
  1. Demonstrated experience in developing national clean cooking, energy transition or comparable energy sector strategies.
  2. Demonstrated experience in clean cooking technologies, markets, value chains and energy access planning.
  3. Experience in policy, regulatory and institutional analysis in the energy sector.
  4. Experience in undertaking household and institutional energy demand assessments, market analysis and consumer research.
  5. Demonstrated experience in investment planning, financial modelling, climate finance and carbon finance for energy access or clean cooking programmes.
  6. Demonstrated experience integrating gender equality, social inclusion and stakeholder engagement into energy sector assignments.
  7. Experience undertaking similar assignments in Sub-Saharan Africa, preferably Southern Africa.
  8. Experience working with governments, development partners or World Bank-financed projects.
  9.  Experience in developing women’s entrepreneurship programme frameworks, including business support models and financing/incubation pathways in the energy sector.
  1. Consultants may associate with other consultants to enhance their qualifications. Where firms are associating, the submission must include verifiable evidence of association from all parties. Experience and qualifications of parent or subsidiary firms will not be considered for evaluation.

 

  1. All submissions from consulting firms shall be in the English language.

 

  1. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.15 to 3.16 of the seventh edition of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers dated September 2025 setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

  1. The Consultant(s) shall be evaluated and a maximum of eight (8) will be shortlisted based on general qualifications, experience and capability. Shortlisted Consultants will subsequently have their RFPs evaluated in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based (QCBS) selection method as per the seventh edition of Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers dated September 2025.

 

  1. Interested eligible consultants may obtain further information by sending an email to the address below or visiting during office hours from 10.00 to 16.00 hrs. The Terms of Reference for the proposed consulting services can be downloaded from the Eswatini Electricity Company TERMS_OF_REFERENCE_CLEAN_COOKING_FINAL.pdf
  2. Expression of interest must be delivered in a written form by e-mail to the address below no later than 11H00 ON  10 September 2026

Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience Program Using the Multiphase Programmatic Approach (P180127)

 

PEDIDO DE MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE

(SERVIÇOS DE CONSULTORIA - SELEÇÃO DE CONSULTORES INDIVIDUAIS)

 

 

PAÍS: São Tomé e Príncipe

 

PROJETO: Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience Program Using the Multiphase Programmatic Approach.

 

Título da consultoria: Contratação de um (1) Consultor Nacional para Formação em Prevenção e controlo de infeção no laboratório associado à resistência antimicrobiana.

 

Ref. Nº: 47/C/HERR/2026

 

O Governo da República Democrática de S. Tomé e Príncipe, através do Ministério da Economia e Finanças, recebeu um finaciamento da Associação Internacional para o Desenvolvimento (IDA), para apoiar a implemantação do Projeto Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience Program Using the Multiphase Programmatic Approach (HERR), e pretende utilizar parte deste recurso para a contratação de serviços de consultoria.

 

O serviço de consultoria consiste na contratação de um (1) Consultor Nacional para Formação em Prevenção e controlo de infeção no laboratório associado à resistência antimicrobiana.

 

 Objetivos da consultoria

Os principais objetivos da consultoria são:

  1. Selecionar um(a) especialista experiente para prestar apoio técnico especializado.
  2. Capacitar os técnicos do Laboratório Nacional de Referência (LNR), assegurando a transferência efetiva de metodologias modernas de controlo de infeção e vigilância da RAM.

O Termo de Referência (TdR) poderá ser solicitado através dos seguintes endereços eletrónicos:

 saude_regional.procurement@afap.st / dg.procurement@afap.st. 

A Agência Fiduciária de Administração de Projetos (AFAP) convida consultores individuais elegíveis (Consultores) a manifestarem o seu interesse na prestação dos serviços, mediante a submissão de uma Carta de Intenção, documento de identificação, Curriculum Vitae atualizado e assinado, e os respetivos comprovativos de formação académica.

Os consultores interessados deverão fornecer informações que demonstrem possuir as qualificações e experiências necessárias para executar os serviços, em conformidade com o Termo de Referência (TdR).

O Consultor deverá possuir as seguintes qualificações mínimas:

  1. Formação Académica
  • Licenciatura em Ciências Biomédicas, Microbiologia, Análises Clínicas, Medicina, Saúde Pública ou áreas estritamente afins.
  • Pós-graduação ou Especialização (Mestrado, Doutoramento ou Curso de Especialização Avançada) em Microbiologia Clínica, Prevenção e Controlo de Infeção (PCI), Biossegurança Laboratorial ou Vigilância da Resistência Antimicrobiana (RAM) constituirá uma vantagem competitiva relevante.

 

  1. Experiência Profissional
  • Mínimo de 5 (cinco) anos de experiência profissional comprovada no domínio do diagnóstico laboratorial microbiológico.
  • Experiência prática consolidada na facilitação de ações de formação de curta ou média duração direcionadas a profissionais da área médica e de saúde.
  • Comprovada experiência de trabalho no desenvolvimento ou implementação de programas de Prevenção e Controlo de Infeção (PCI).
  • Experiência prática em recolha, transporte, processamento e análise microbiológica de amostras de matriz ambiental e hospitalar.
  • Conhecimento robusto das dinâmicas e metodologias de vigilância epidemiológica e laboratorial da Resistência Antimicrobiana (RAM).
  • Familiaridade comprovada com as diretrizes e manuais da Organização Mundial da Saúde (OMS), bem como com os normativos e protocolos de biossegurança vigentes.

 

  1. Competência Técnica
  • Excelente capacidade pedagógica, de facilitação e de formação contínua de adultos (andragogia).
  • Elevado rigor e competência técnica em redação científica e elaboração de relatórios profissionais.
  • Excelentes capacidades de comunicação interpessoal, facilidade de articulação institucional e aptidão para trabalhar de forma colaborativa com equipas multidisciplinares.

 

  1. Competência Linguística
  • Excelente domínio da língua portuguesa, capacidade de comunicar em inglês e /ou francês.

 

Chama-se a atenção dos Consultores interessados para o disposto na Seção III, parágrafos 3.14, 3.16 e 3.17 do Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários de Financiamento de Projetos de Investimento (FPI) do Banco Mundial, edição de setembro de 2025, que estabelece a política do Banco Mundial relativa a conflitos de interesse.

A seleção será realizada de acordo com o método de Seleção de Consultor Individual (Individual Consultant Selection – ICS), conforme previsto no Regulamento de Aquisições do Banco Mundial para Mutuários de Financiamento de Projetos de Investimento (FPI) do Banco Mundial, edição de setembro de 2025.

dg.procurement@afap.st / saude_regional.procurement@afap.st ou entregues presencialmente no endereço indicado abaixo, com a seguinte referência :

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST
(INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT)

The Government of Indonesia
Global Environment Facility Indonesia Sustainable Cities Impact Project
Grant No.: TF B8114
Assignment Title: Transportation Specialist
(National Consultant)
Reference No.: ID-TRANSPORT - BAPPENAS-561678-CS-INDV

The Government of Indonesia, through the Ministry of National Development Planning/National Development Planning Agency (Bappenas), has received grant funding from the Global Environment Facility (GEF) Sustainable Cities Impact Project (SCIP) through the World Bank. Part of this funding is allocated for individual consultant services.

The Individual Consultant – Transportation Specialist will be assigned to the Directorate of Connectivity and Logistics Infrastructure, Bappenas, and will work closely with the team of Individual Consultants in providing technical guidance and supervision for the development of the Sustainable Urban Mobility Plan (SUMP) in Balikpapan and Palembang, which is carried out by the contracted consulting firms.

The main tasks of the Individual Consultant include:

  1. Task 1: Technical Oversight and Advisory of SUMP Development, Including Knowledge Integration and Cross-Cutting Inputs.
    1. Provide technical advisory support to the Balikpapan and Palembang SUMP development process by integrating relevant lessons learned from previous studies, national programs, and international best practices into the consulting firms' work.
    2. Provide technical review and supervision of the consulting firms' data collection activities, survey implementation, and analytical methodologies, including household surveys, O/D Matrix, four-step transport model, level of service (LOS), non-motorized transport (NMT), travel demand management (TDM), and other technical analyses to ensure methodological soundness and analytical consistency
    3. Provide strategic inputs on cross-cutting topics including, but not limited to, multimodal integration, feeder concepts (e.g., the Palembang LRT feeder network), angkot/BRT reform, non-motorized transport (NMT) and accessibility, transport demand management (TDM), and land use/transit-oriented development (TOD) integration. Recommendations shall support the consulting firms and the Directorate in strengthening the technical direction and strategic coherence of each city's SUMP as it develops.
  2. Task 2: SUMP Development Deliverables Oversight.
    1. Conduct oversight of the SUMP consulting firms' deliverables (step 1 until step 15) for Balikpapan and Palembang to ensure completeness and consistency against the required deliverable items set out in each firm's Term of Reference, including data collection and survey outputs, transport modelling methodology and outputs, existing conditions assessment, vision development, policy measures, investment prioritization, and implementation strategy.
    2. Maintain and update a consolidated deliverables checklist tracking the status of each required item (submitted / complete / pending / needs revision) for both cities, and provide written technical comments where gaps, delays, or inconsistencies are identified.

To support the main tasks, the Consultant may undertake the following supporting activities, but not limited to:

  1. Task 3: Advisory, Capacity Building and Coordination Support to the Directorate.
    1. Capacity building and technical guidance of the Directorate. Work alongside the team of Individual Consultants to deliver technical guidance and capacity improvement to the Directorate in key areas such as integrated transport planning through sustainable urban mobility plan principles, infrastructure investment planning, creative financing, Traffic Demand Management (TDM), and development of Integrated Transport Authority (ITA) frameworks.
    2. Coordination of GEF Indonesia SCIP Component 2 Activities. Support the coordination and monitoring of activities under GEF Indonesia SCIP Component 2 related to SUMP development, ensuring consistency between the outputs of the consulting firm and the overall program objectives.

The individual consultant services are expected to start in September 2026 and perform the service for 4 months.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found in the following link: https://link.bappenas.go.id/08192026034658

The Directorate of Connectivity and Logistics Infrastructure at the Ministry of National Development Planning/National Development Planning Agency now invites eligible individual consultant (“Consultant”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultant should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are the relevant experience of the individual consultant in:

REQUIRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

  • Essential Qualification
  1. Minimum of a Master's degree in transportation system, transportation engineering, civil engineering with transport specialization, or a related field including urban planning, with at least 1 year of relevant work experience in urban transportation planning, transport modelling, or sustainable urban mobility; OR a Bachelor's degree in civil engineering or urban planning with at least 4 years of relevant work experience in urban transportation planning, transport modelling, or sustainable urban mobility;
  2. Demonstrated working experience in environmental and/or social safeguarding aspects of infrastructure or urban development projects (e.g., familiarity with donor safeguard frameworks such as the World Bank's Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), AMDAL, or equivalent);
  3. Familiarity with the Indonesian urban transport planning context, including relevant national policies and regulations governing urban mobility and public transport;
  4. Proficient in performing quantitative and qualitative data analysis in transportation sector and demonstrating strong communication and writing skills in professional English (proven by policy papers/books/studies/journals/research/essay/report/ToR sample in English) and Bahasa Indonesia;
  • Additional Qualifications (an advantage)
  1. Has experience in a minimum of one (1) SUMP/Pre-FS/FS project (proven by CV and supporting document(s) such as contracts, acknowledgment letter, or other related documents);
  2. Demonstrated strong familiarity with Sustainable Urban Mobility Plan (SUMP) development principles – including data collection and analysis, scenario development, and staged implementation;
  3. Demonstrated hands-on experience in at least three of the following: travel demand modeling (including four-step model application), travel survey design and analysis (household, roadside, on-board), public transport network planning and analysis, NMT planning, and travel demand management;
  4. Experience working on national/international development agency operations such as Ministry of National Development Planning (Bappenas)/Ministry of Transportation/World Bank/Asian Development Bank/USAID/GIZ/GCF/KIAT, etc.

The selected individual consultant will be based in the Jakarta (Indonesia) office.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers July 2016, revised November 2017, July 2018, November 2020, and September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours (09.00 to 17.00 GMT+7).

Interested applicant must submit the comprehensive curriculum vitae of individual consultant before August 26, 2026 at 16.00 WIB to the following address:

Directorate Connectivity and Logistics Infrastructure

Ministry of National Development Planning/Bappenas

Email: handhi.adiputra@bappenas.go.id

procnotices.contact_address: Villa Somalia, Mogadishu
procnotices.contact_organization: Federal Government of Somalia Ministry of Finance
procnotices.notice_text:
Recurrent Cost and Reform Financing Project (RCRFP III)

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (REOI) (CONSULTING SERVICES) FIRMS SELECTION

COUNTRY:                           Federal Republic of Somalia (FGS)

NAME OF PROJECT          Somalia Recurrent Cost & Reform Financing (RCRF) Project - Phase III                                  

PROJECT ID                          P173731

Grant No.                            IDA-E3120

Assignment Title: Gap Assessment of Payroll Enrollment and Payment Controls in Federal Member States - Reference No: SO-MOF-564846-CS-CQS

Place of assignment:  Mogadishu and other Federal Member States of Somalia

Background

I. The Federal Government of Somalia, through the Ministry of Finance, has received financing from the World Bank for the Somalia Recurrent Cost and Reform Financing Project that supports the FGS and eligible Federal Member States (FMS) in strengthening resource management systems, the intergovernmental fiscal relations, and service delivery in health and education. The project disburses financing against Performance-Based Conditions (PBCs), under which payment follows independently verified evidence that agreed reform milestones have been achieved, rather than against inputs alone.

II. The Government intends to apply part of the proceeds in the Procurement of Consulting Gap Assessment of Payroll Enrollment and Payment Controls in Federal Member States.

III. The Ministry of Finance now invites eligible firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.  The short-listing criteria are as follows:

A. Core Business and Years in Business: the firm must be a legally registered entity with a core business focus on public financial management, HR, governance, institutional, regulatory, or public sector reform. The firm must have been in operation for at least ten (10) years.

B. Relevant Experience: The firm should demonstrate experience in PFM, HR, governance, Institutional, financial, or regulatory review/reform process, with successful execution of at least two (2) similar assignments. For each referenced assignment, provide evidence related to the assignment, including title, scope of work, client name, address, and contact details, duration, and contract value.

C. Technical and managerial capacity: The firm should demonstrate sufficient technical and managerial capacity to carry out the assignment.; and

D. The technical and managerial capability of the firm. (Provide the structure of the organization, general qualifications, and the number of key staff and their qualifications.

IV. Terms of Reference:

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) can be found at the following website: www.mof.gov.so  or it can be forwarded to the applicant upon submission of the application to the address indicated below.

V. Selection Method:

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to section III, para 3.14, 3.16 & 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Projects Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, "Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers" July 2016, revised November 2017 revised August 2018, November 2020, 2023 and 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest and eligibility.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations. Interested Consultants may obtain further information at the address below during office hours from 8:30 am to 3.30 pm Mogadishu time (Excluding public holidays).

Expressions of interest (EOI) should be delivered by e-mail below indicating “SO-MOF-564846-CS-CQS Procurement of Consulting Gap Assessment of Payroll Enrollment and Payment Controls in Federal Member States); on the email subject to the address below by   2nd  September 2026 at 12:00 Hours (Mogadishu Time)

Email address:  rcrfrecruitment@mof.gov.so

Project Implementation Unit,

Ministry of Finance of Federal Government of Somalia,

Objectives of the Assignment

 

To lead and implement the communication and public relations (PR) components of the regional One Health program, ensuring unified messaging, stakeholder engagement, and media visibility through both digital and traditional communication channels.

The PR consultant will be responsible for the following:

  • Develop and implement the Regional One Health Communication Strategy, in coordination with PR manager, Project coordinator, national focal points and WB team.
  • Develop a brand identity and maintain visual consistency across all communication materials.
  • Prepare and implement a publication and content calendar, aligned with project milestones and thematic priorities.

 

  1. Media & Public Relations
     
  • Develop and implement a media outreach plan, covering traditional (TV, radio, print) and online outlets across the region.
  • Build and maintain a media contact database of relevant journalists and editorial contacts in participating countries.
  • Invite and coordinate media participation in project events, including forums, launches, consultations, and training.
  • Prepare press kits for events, including press releases, background briefs, speaker bios, visual materials, and quotes.
  • Draft and disseminate press releases, opinion articles, interviews, and news stories in collaboration with technical teams and national stakeholders.
  • Organize and moderate media briefings and press conferences as needed.
  • Liaise directly with journalists and editors to support coverage of project activities and secure interviews with project representatives.
  • Conduct ongoing media monitoring and analysis, collecting and archiving published materials and tracking media exposure on monthly basis and present this analysis to the project coordinator.
  • Prepare quarterly media monitoring reports, assessing visibility, tone, outreach scope, and communication impact.

 

  1.  Digital Communication & Social Media
     
  • Design and manage regional social media campaigns, including content planning, visual creation, and performance tracking.
  • Contribute to the Central Asian One Health Information Portal by uploading communications products and ensuring regular updates.
  • Use interactive tools (surveys, infographics, Q&A sessions) to increase engagement with the general public and stakeholder communities.
  • Coordinate with national focal points/partners to collect, verify, and package news, success stories, photos, quotes and event updates for publication.
  • Draft, design, schedule and publish posts (RU/EN) across agreed channels (e.g., Facebook/Instagram/LinkedIn/Telegram), including basic community management (replying/moderation per agreed SOP).
  • Maintain a shared content pipeline (news intake form + approvals tracker) and a monthly/weekly publishing plan

 

  1. Visual Design & Content Production (In-house)

 

  • Consultant is responsible for independent development of visual materials for the project, including (but not limited to): web-banners, website sliders/covers, social media templates, story/reel covers, infographics, event visuals, roll-up/banner layouts, presentation templates, news cards, email headers, etc.
  • Consultant must provide editable source files for all designs (e.g., CDR/.PSD/.AI/.INDD + exported .PNG/.JPG/.PDF) and maintain an organized archive (cloud folder) with version control.
  • Consultant ensures brand consistency across all materials

 

  1. Coordination with Contractors and Content Production
     
  • When external production is required (photo/video/printing/large-scale creative), Consultant prepares ToRs and supervises contractors; however, routine graphic design and digital visuals are produced by the Consultant in-house.
  • Coordinate the production of visual and promotional content (banners, roll-ups, branded merchandise, video explainers, photos, educational infographics).
  • Oversee venue branding and decoration for events in accordance with project identity standards.
  • Supervise contractors to ensure quality, timeliness, and consistency in all visual communications deliverables.

 

  1. Capacity Building and Training
  • Conduct a needs assessment on communications capacity among project partners.
  • Develop and deliver training for CAREC staff, national stakeholders, and focal points on effective communication, media engagement, and public messaging.
  • Support crisis communication preparedness, including simulations and guidance development.

 

  1. Monitoring and Evaluation
  • Define KPIs for communication activities and develop simple tracking tools (e.g., dashboards).
  • Conduct quarterly assessments of campaigns and PR performance; propose adjustments.
  • Contribute to donor visibility reports, CAREC publications, and knowledge products based on communication outcomes.

 

Assignment Duration

 

The assignment will last for 12 months, beginning from contract signing. Extension may be considered based on project dynamics.

 

Reporting

 

The PR consultant reports to the CAREC OH Project Coordinator and works closely with technical teams, the M&E specialist, and national communication focal points.

 

Assignment Conditions

  • The Consultant shall use their own hardware and software and maintain valid licenses for required design tools (e.g., CorelDRAW, Adobe Photoshop/Illustrator/InDesign and/or equivalent).
  • All costs related to creation of digital visual materials (software subscriptions, fonts, plugins, stock assets) are covered by the Consultant and included in the fee, unless explicitly pre-approved in writing by CAREC.
  • Printing and physical production (e.g., printing roll-ups/banners/merch) is not covered by the Consultant unless separately agreed and budgeted; Consultant provides print-ready files and technical specs.

 

Assignment Location

 

CAREC Headquarters in Almaty, Kazakhstan or one of the Central Asian countries with the possibility of remote work, with occasional travel within Central Asia for event support and stakeholder engagement.

 

Qualifications

 

Education

  • University degree in Communications, Public Relations, Journalism, Marketing, or related field.

 

Experience

  • At least 5 years of experience in PR, media relations, or strategic communications for international/regional development programs.
  • Strong background in managing social media campaigns, organizing press events, and working with multimedia contractors.
  • Previous experience in working with donors such as the World Bank, WHO, or FAO is a strong asset.

 

Skills

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English and Russian.
  • Strong media writing, storytelling, and content creation abilities.
  • Proficiency in design tools (e.g., Canva, Adobe Creative Suite, CorelDRAW,Adobe Photoshop/Illustrator (plus optional Figma/After Effects) and media monitoring software.
  • Organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Cultural sensitivity and ability to work with diverse stakeholders
  • Portfolio required demonstrating banner/social/event design.

 

Detailed Terms of reference is available at the link.

Interested candidates are required to CV and cover letter to smustafin@carececo.org with copy to okravtsova@carececo.org  not later than 04 March, 2026.  

 

Please be sure to indicate PR consultant in the subject line of the email.

procnotices.notice_text:
Introduction

On June 22, 2025, the World Bank Board of Executive Directors approved an allocation of US$3.45 million from the International Development Association (IDA) to finance the first phase of the ONE HEALTH FOR PANDEMIC PREVENTION, FOOD SYSTEMS RESILIENCE, AND ECOSYSTEM HEALTH IN CENTRAL ASIA PROJECT. This approved financing to be implemented by the Regional Environmental Center for Central Asia (CAREC) for day-to-day regional coordination and implementation.

Project Description

The objective of the Project is to establish the capacity of the Regional One Health Coordination Structure in managing priority zoonotic diseases, antimicrobial resistance, and food safety issues in Central Asia through a regional One Health approach.

The Project constitutes a phase of the MPA Program, and consists of the following parts:

Part 1. Establishing One Health Governance.

Technical assistance and the provision of goods for:

establishing and maintaining the Regional One Health Coordination Structure;

developing Regional One Health Action Plan(s);

establishing the Central Asia One Health Portal;

developing and implementing a regional One Health communication and stakeholder engagement strategy;

organizing regular consultations and meetings with key stakeholders;

developing a regional laboratory network strategy; and

conducting regulatory assessments and reviews relevant to regional One Health issues to suggest areas for policy improvement.

Part 2. Enhancing One Health Knowledge and Workforce Capacity.

Technical assistance and the provision of goods for establishing an institutional mechanism for knowledge development and exchange, as well as technical capacity development at the regional level. Activities will include:

conducting regional risk assessments on priority regional threats from zoonoses, antimicrobial resistance and food risks;

conducting regional or cross-border outbreak response exercises;

establishing a regional training platform as part of the Central Asia One Health Portal; and

organizing targeted training and capacity building activities for key professions in the veterinary, human health and environment sectors in participating countries.

Part 3. Project Management, Monitoring and Evaluation, and Learning.

Technical assistance and the provision of goods for project management activities, including:

the creation of a monitoring and evaluation framework; and

communications and supporting systems to enhance learning and tracking of effectiveness of Recipient-managed One Health activities.

In accordance with the Financing and Operating Agreements and the WB requirements, the project is subject to independent external audit to be conducted after the end of each financial year (or another period agreed with the WB) throughout the project period. The main objective of the external audit is to check whether the donor funds are used as designated and express an independent opinion on the project financial reports for the reporting financial year.

 

Objective

The objective of the audit of the Project Financial Statements (PFS) is to enable the auditor to express a professional opinion on the financial position of the Project as of the end of each fiscal year and on the Project’s sources and uses of funds for the respective reporting period, in accordance with the applicable financial reporting framework.

The audit shall cover the period from June 24, 2025 to July 31, 2027, and shall continue annually until the Disbursement Deadline Date of November 30, 2027, as applicable.

The Project’s books of account shall be maintained in accordance with sound accounting practices and shall provide the basis for the preparation of the Project Financial Statements. The accounting records shall reflect all financial transactions related to the Project.

Audit Periods

  • The first audit shall cover the period from June 24, 2025 to December 31, 2025.
  • The second audit shall cover the period from January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2026.
  • The final audit shall cover the period from January 1, 2027 to July 31, 2027 and include grace period.

 

 

Responsibility for preparation of financial statements

The project’s management is responsible for the preparation of financial statements, including the maintenance of adequate accounting records and internal controls, the selection and application of accounting policies, the safeguarding of the assets of the project, and adequate disclosure.  As part of the audit process, the auditor will request from management written confirmation concerning representations made to us in connection with the audit.

Scope

The audit will be conducted in accordance with International Standards on Auditing. Those Standards require that the auditor plans and performs the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatements. An audit includes examining, on a test basis, evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements. An audit also includes assessing the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall financial statement presentation.

In complying with International Standards on Auditing, the auditor is expected to pay particular attention to the following matters, including special considerations for public sector entities:

  1. In planning and performing the audit to reduce audit risk to an acceptably low level, the auditor should consider the risks of material misstatements in the financial statements due to fraud, as required by International Standard on Auditing 240: The Auditor’s Responsibilities Relating to Fraud in an Audit of Financial Statements.
  2. When designing and performing audit procedures and in evaluating and reporting the results thereof, the auditor should recognize that noncompliance by the entity with laws and regulations may materially affect the financial statements, as required by International Standard on Auditing 250: Consideration of Laws and Regulations in an Audit of Financial Statements.
  3. The auditor should communicate audit matters of governance interest arising from the audit of financial statements to those charged with governance of an entity, as required by International Standard on Auditing 260: Communication with those Charged with Governance.
  4. The auditor should appropriately communicate to those charged with governance and to management any deficiencies in internal control that the auditor has identified in an audit of financial statements, as required by International Standard on Auditing 265: Communicating Deficiencies in Internal Control to Those Charged with Governance and Management.
  5. To reduce audit risk to an acceptably low level, the auditor should determine overall responses to assessed risks at the financial statement level, and should design and perform further audit procedures to respond to assessed risks at the assertion level, as required by International Standard on Auditing 330: The Auditor’s Responses to Assessed Risks.
  6. When certain aspects of an entity’s operations are performed by a third-party service provider, the auditor is expected to include an understanding and assessment of the internal control environment of the service provider during the audit process, as required by International Standard on Auditing 402: Audit Considerations Relating to an Entity Using a Service Organization.
  7. As part of the audit process, the auditor is expected to obtain written representations from management and, where appropriate, those charged with governance, as required by International Standard on Auditing 580: Written Representations. 
  8. When the external auditor decides to use the work of an entity’s internal audit function to modify the nature or timing, or reduce the extent, of audit procedures to be performed directly by the external auditor, the determination shall be in accordance with International Standard on Auditing 610: Using the Work of Internal Auditors.   In determining whether to use the work of an auditor’s expert or the extent to which the work of an auditor’s expert is adequate for audit purposes, the determination shall be made in accordance with International Standard on Auditing 620: Using the Work of an Auditor’s Expert.  

In evidencing compliance with agreed project financing arrangements, the auditor is expected to carry out tests to confirm that:

  1. All external funds have been used in accordance with the conditions of the relevant financing agreements, with due attention to economy and efficiency, and only for the purposes for which the financing was provided. Relevant financing agreements include financing agreement GRANT NUMBER TF-C7896.
  2. Goods, works, and services financed have been procured in accordance with relevant financing agreements,[1] including specific provisions of the World Bank Procurement Guidelines.[2]
  3. All necessary supporting documents, records, and accounts have been maintained in respect of all project activities, including expenditures reported using Statements of Expenditure (SOE) The auditor is expected to verify that respective reports issued during the period were in agreement with the underlying books of account.

Project financial statements

The auditor should verify that the financial statements have been prepared in accordance with International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS)”Financial Reporting Under the Cash Basis of Accounting “cash-basis method. The financial statements should include:

 

) A statement of sources and uses of funds;

 

b) Accounting policies and explanatory notes[3] (including additional accounting policies and disclosures), which will include:

- Statement of Financial position;

- Statements of Expenditure used as the basis for submission of withdrawal applications in the notes;

- A statement on the Designated account in the notes; and

- When the entity makes publicly available its approved budget, a comparison of budget and actual amounts either as a separate additional financial statement or as a budget column in the financial statements

Review of Statements of Expenditure The auditor is required to audit all SOE submitted to the World Bank in support of requests for periodic replenishment of the project designated account(s). Expenditures should be examined for eligibility based on criteria defined in the terms of the financing agreement and detailed in the Project Appraisal Document. The auditor should report any ineligible expenditures identified as having been included in withdrawal applications and reimbursed. The auditor should pay particular attention to whether:

  1. the Summary Reports (or SOEs) have been prepared in accordance with the provisions of the relevant financing agreement;
  2. expenditures have been made wholly and necessarily for the realization of project objectives;
  3. information and explanation necessary for the purpose of the audit have been obtained;
  4. supporting records and documents necessary for the purpose of the audit have been retained, and
  5. the Summary Reports (or SOEs) can be relied upon to support the related withdrawal applications.

Review of designated accounts

During the audit of the project financial statements, the auditor is required to review the activities of the project’s designated account(s). Activities to be examined will include deposits received, payments made, interest earned, and reconciliation of period-end balances.

Audit Reports

Audit opinion

The auditor will issue an audit opinion on project financial statements. The auditor’s opinion shall be based on an evaluation of the conclusions drawn from the audit evidence obtained and shall be expressed clearly through a written report that also describes the basis for that opinion. The audit report shall be prepared in accordance with International Standard on Auditing 700: Forming an Opinion and Reporting on Financial Statements. 

A modified audit opinion shall be rendered in the financial statements when the auditor concludes, on the basis of the audit evidence obtained, that the financial statements as a whole are not free from material misstatement; or the auditor is unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence to conclude that the financial statements as a whole are free from material misstatement. Modified audit opinions shall be in accordance with International Standard on Auditing 705: Modifications to the Opinion in the Independent Auditor’s Report.

The auditor will include emphasis of matter paragraphs or other matter paragraphs in the audit opinion where the auditor, having formed an opinion on the financial statements, seeks to draw users’ attention, when in the auditor’s judgment it is necessary to do so, by way of clear additional communication in the auditor’s report. The paragraphs will refer to either a matter that, although appropriately presented or disclosed in the financial statements, is of such importance that it is fundamental to users’ understanding of the financial statements; or as appropriate, any other matter that is relevant to users’ understanding of the audit, the auditor’s responsibilities, or the auditor’s report. This form of opinion will be presented in accordance with International Standard on Auditing 706: Emphasis of Matter Paragraphs or Other Matter Paragraphs in the Independent Auditor’s Report.

Other audit reports

In addition to the audit opinion(s), the auditor will also, either in the audit report or in the report to management:

  1. provide comments and observations on the accounting records, systems, and controls that were examined during the course of the audit;
  2. identify specific deficiencies and areas of weakness in systems and controls and make recommendation for their improvement;
  3. report on instances of noncompliance with the terms of the financial agreement(s);
  4. quantify and report expenditures that are considered to be ineligible and either paid out of the designated account(s) or claimed from the World Bank;
  5. communicate matters that have come to attention during the audit that might have a significant impact on the implementation of the project;
  6. draw to the borrower’s attention any other matters that the auditor considers pertinent; and
  7. responses from management, including implemented and proposed remedial actions.

If, during the audit nothing has come to the attention that the auditor considers pertinent to be brought to the attention of the borrower, and a management letter is therefore not prepared, the auditor will issue a letter stating this.

The auditor’s opinion on the financial statements and management letter should be received by the Bank no later than of 30 June 2026.

Public Disclosure

In accordance with "The World Bank (the Bank) Policy on Access to Information", the Bank requires that the recipient makes project audited financial statements publicly available in a timely fashion and manner acceptable to the Bank. In addition, following the Bank’s formal receipt of these financial statements from the borrower, the Bank makes them available to the public in accordance with this policy.

Management Letters and unaudited financial statements (e.g. Interim Financial Reports) are not considered to be a part of the definition of the audited financial statements for the purposes of disclosure.

Only in exceptional cases the Bank may agree — i.e., when the audited financial statements contain proprietary or commercially sensitive information — that the borrower or designated project entity may be exempted from disclosing the full set of audited financial statements, but is still required to disclose an abridged version of them in a form acceptable to the Bank.  Exceptions are approved by World Bank management.

General

The auditor is entitled to unlimited access to all information and explanations considered necessary to facilitate the audit, including legal documents, project preparation and supervision reports, reports of reviews and investigations, correspondences, and credit account information. The auditor may also seek written confirmation of amounts disbursed and outstanding in the Bank records.

The auditor is encouraged to meet and discuss audit-related matters, including input to the audit plan, with the World Bank project task team.

It is highly desirable that the auditor reviews the Bank's financial reporting and auditing requirements contained in Operational Policies OP 10.00 Investment Project Financing;. The auditor should also be familiar with the 2017 Bank’s Disbursement Guidelines for Investment Project Financing and the Loan Handbook for World Bank Borrowers (the Loan Handbook) and Financial Monitoring Reports for World Bank-Financed Projects: Guidelines for Borrowers, November 30, 2001; and World Bank Procurement Guidelines.

This term of engagement will remain effective for future fiscal years unless it is terminated, amended or superseded.

 

[1] Depending on the complexity of procurement activities, the auditor may consider involving technical experts during the audit engagement. When such experts are involved, the auditor is expected to comply with provisions of International Standard on Auditing 620: Using the Work of an Expert. Consideration of using of the work of experts should be brought to the early attention of the borrower and the World Bank for mutual agreement and appropriate guidance.

[2] See Guidelines: Procurement Under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits, Revised July 2014 and Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants by World Bank Borrowers, Revised July 2014.

[3] The explanations should include a reconciliation between the amounts shown by the project received from the World Bank and those paid by the World Bank, as well as the Funds Flow Statement of the Designated Account.

Solicitação de Manifestação de Interesse – SMI Nº 0012/2026

 

A FUNDAÇÃO GETULIO VARGAS, ou simplesmente FGV, torna público que está aberto o prazo para consultores não individuais (pessoas jurídicas) elegíveis interessados na apresentação de MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE, com vistas à consultoria não individual especializada em mapeamento participativo e diagnóstico socioambiental da atividade pesqueira na Floresta Nacional de Tefé. Os consultores não individuais interessados deverão demonstrar que são qualificados e que têm a experiência para desempenhar o serviço, conforme descrito no Termo de Referência, disponível em: https://asl-brasil.fgv.br/compras-e-contratacoes

 

           As Manifestações de Interesse deverão ser enviadas até dia 28/08/2026, às 23h59, para o e-mail  asl2.compras@fgv.br. As Manifestações deverão estar identificadas como SMI Nº 0012/2026 – MAPEAMENTO PARTICIPATIVO–FLONA TEFÉ. A consultoria não individual (pessoa jurídica) deverá demonstrar capacidade para atuar em mapeamento participativo e diagnóstico socioambiental da atividade pesqueira na Floresta Nacional de Tefé, garantindo que as atividades ocorram conforme o planejamento, que engloba levantamento de dados primários e secundários, mapeamento participativo das áreas de uso pesqueiro, condução de oficinas participativas e sistematização de diagnóstico socioambiental da atividade pesqueira. A consultoria não individual (pessoa jurídica) interessada deverá apresentar os currículos da equipe técnica proposta, o portfólio institucional e demais documentos de acordo com os requisitos definidos no Termo de Referência.

 

Para fins desta Manifestação de Interesse, a consultoria não individual (pessoa jurídica) interessada deverá comprovar, no mínimo, a seguinte qualificação:

i. Experiência de pelo menos 3 (três) anos de execução de trabalhos na área socioambiental na região do Mosaico do Baixo Rio Negro e/ou em outras áreas com reconhecimento de gestão integrada na Amazônia, tais como Reserva da Biosfera da Amazônia Central, Sítio Ramsar Rio Negro, Sítio Ramsar Rio Juruá e Complexo de Conservação da Amazônia Central - Sítio do Patrimônio Mundial Natural da Amazônia.

ii. Experiência de pelo menos 3 (três) anos, na atuação junto a povos e comunidades tradicionais, preferencialmente na Amazônia, com foco em cadeias produtivas e exploração de recursos pesqueiros. Será considerado um diferencial a experiência de atuação em Unidades de Conservação Federal.

iii. Experiência de pelo menos 3 (três) anos, na realização de mapeamentos participativos, através de condução e mediação de oficinas participativas.

iv. Experiência de pelo menos 3 (três) anos, na elaboração de documentos técnicos que identifiquem desafios, potencialidades e recomendações para as cadeias produtivas.

 

Esta Solicitação de Manifestação de Interesse não pressupõe qualquer compromisso de contratação. Os(as) consultores(as) não individuais (pessoas jurídicas) elegíveis serão avaliados(as) de acordo com as normas do “Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários de Operações de Financiamento de Projetos de Investimento, edição de setembro de 2023”.

 

Informações adicionais sobre o processo seletivo poderão ser solicitadas pelo endereço eletrônico asl2.compras@fgv.br

 

A Fundação Getúlio Vargas entrará em contato somente com os(as) consultores(as) não individuais (pessoas jurídicas) elegíveis para a próxima etapa do processo.

procnotices.bid_description: MEAL Officer for Bulsho Somaliland- Project Implementation Unit (PIU)
procnotices.contact_address: Near the Presidential Palace, behind the Ministry of Livestock, Hargeisa, Somaliland.
procnotices.contact_organization: Ministry of Local Governments and Urban Development
procnotices.notice_text:
GOVERNMENT OF SOMALILAND

MINISTRY OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT (MoLGUD)

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (REOI)

INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION

Country: Somaliland
Project ID: P508408
Project Name: Bulsho Project – Strengthening Community Institutions for Social Cohesion, Inclusion and Resilience
Consulting Service: PIU Bulsho Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) Officer
Selection Type: Individual Consultant

Reference: SO-MOLGUD-567776-CS-INDV
Duty Station: Hargeisa, Somaliland, with travel to project regions and districts
Duration: 12 months, renewable subject to satisfactory performance
Application Deadline: September 3, 2026, at 4:00 PM Hargeisa Time

1. BACKGROUND

The Ministry of Local Government and Urban Development (MoLGUD) of the Government of Somaliland is implementing the World Bank-financed Bulsho Project – Strengthening Community Institutions for Social Cohesion, Inclusion and Resilience (P508408).

The main objective of the Bulsho Program is to strengthen community and local institutions for improved social cohesion, inclusion, and resilience. The Program places citizens and communities at the center of government action and seeks to strengthen service delivery, local governance, citizen engagement, and the social contract between communities and government.

To support implementation of the Bulsho Project, the Government of Somaliland, through MoLGUD, intends to recruit a qualified and experienced Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) Officer as part of the Project Implementation Unit (PIU).

2. SCOPE OF THE ASSIGNMENT

The PIU Bulsho MEAL Officer will lead the implementation of the Project’s monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning system, ensuring high-quality data collection, validation, analysis, reporting, evidence generation, accountability, and learning in accordance with the Project Appraisal Document (PAD), Project Operations Manual (POM), Results Framework (RF), Monitoring and Evaluation Plan (MEP), and World Bank requirements.

The MEAL Officer will be responsible for monitoring, evaluation and reporting; Management Information System (MIS) and data management; surveys, research and evidence generation; accountability and citizen feedback; learning and knowledge management; data quality assurance; and capacity building. The Officer will also coordinate closely with other PIU members and relevant service providers, including Third-Party Monitoring, Digital Innovation, and Knowledge Management and Research firms.

The detailed scope of services, responsibilities, deliverables, reporting arrangements, and other requirements are provided in the attached Terms of Reference (TOR).

3. QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

The successful candidate shall meet the following minimum qualifications and experience:

  • A Master’s degree from a recognized university in Statistics, Economics, Social Sciences, Development Studies, or a related field.
  • A minimum of seven (7) years of professional experience in Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) for donor-funded projects in fragile or conflict-affected contexts, preferably in Somaliland or the East Africa region.
  • Strong skills and demonstrated experience in quantitative and qualitative data analysis, research, and data visualization.
  • Demonstrated experience with Management Information Systems (MIS), statistical software such as STATA, SPSS or R, and digital data collection tools such as KoboToolbox.
  • Experience in setting up and managing KoboToolbox projects, including form deployment, version control, submission monitoring, and administration of user roles and permissions.
  • Demonstrated experience in Knowledge Management (KM), including developing and curating knowledge products and supporting organizational learning.
  • Proven ability to use M&E and research evidence for adaptive programming, evidence-based decision-making, and continuous improvement of project implementation.
  • Experience working with government institutions, preferably in fragile or conflict-affected settings.
  • Knowledge of World Bank M&E requirements and Results Frameworks is an advantage.
  • Strong understanding of results-based management (RBM), Theory of Change, M&E frameworks, indicators, and qualitative and quantitative research methods.
  • Strong analytical, report-writing, communication, presentation, coordination, planning, and capacity-building skills.
  • Knowledge of Somaliland’s socio-political and institutional context and understanding of cross-cutting issues, including gender, inclusion, and conflict sensitivity.
  • High professional integrity and attention to detail.
  • Excellent command of English and Somali, including reading, writing, communication, and presentation skills.

4. REPORTING AND DURATION

The PIU Bulsho MEAL Officer will report to the Bulsho PIU Project Manager.

The assignment will initially be for 12 months and may be renewed subject to satisfactory performance and project requirements. The duty station is Hargeisa, Somaliland, with travel to project regions and districts.

5. SELECTION METHOD

The Ministry of Local Government and Urban Development (MoLGUD), Government of Somaliland, now invites eligible and qualified Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the above-mentioned services.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Project Financing – Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020 and September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations and applicable Government of Somaliland policies.

6. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS

Interested Consultants should submit:

  1. A detailed and updated Curriculum Vitae (CV), including contact details of three (3) professional referees;
  2. Copies of relevant academic qualification certificates; and
  3. A cover letter outlining the candidate’s relevant experience, qualifications, and suitability for the assignment.

Interested and qualified candidates should submit their applications by email with the subject line:

“Application for PIU Bulsho MEAL Officer – SO-MOLGUD-567776-CS-INDV”

To: bulsho.somaliland@outlook.com
Cc: dg.molgud@sldgov.org

Applications must be received no later than September 3, 2026, at 4:00 PM Hargeisa Time.

 

Attention:

PIU Bulsho Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) Officer Recruitment
Bulsho Project – Strengthening Community Institutions for Social Cohesion, Inclusion and Resilience
Ministry of Local Government and Urban Development (MoLGUD)
Government of Somaliland
Hargeisa, Somaliland

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this REOI.
